title: Protocol for calcium imaging of dorsal and ventral CA1 neurons in head-fixed mice
protocol: Anesthetize the mouse by placing it in an anesthesia induction chamber filled with 3% isoflurane at a rate of 1 L/min for about 5 minutes until the mouse reaches criteria such as relaxation of body and tail muscles, gasping once every second, and no response to toe or tail pinching.
Fix the mouse’s head in the stereotaxic by placing it on the apparatus and securing its head with ear bars.
Set the Homeothermic system temperature to 33.5°C to maintain the mouse's body temperature during surgery.
Trim the hair and incise the skin on top of the head for surgical access.
Disinfect the surgical site with chlorhexidine gluconate solution.
Trim the hair in the designated area with scissors.
Clean the surgical site with chlorhexidine gluconate solution.
Dab the surgical site with lidocaine solution (∼100 μL).
Inject ketoprofen solution via IM (100 μL/g).
Make a 1.2 cm incision along the midline of the skin.
Apply eye lubricant to the mouse’s eyes.
Gently push the skin to the left and right with sterilized cotton swabs to widen the incision.
Clean the exposed skull with a sterilized dry cotton swab and a saline-dipped cotton swab.
Level the skull.
Fasten a 22–26 gauge needle to the stereotaxic holder.
Put ink on the tip of the needle.
Gently touch the bregma and lambda with the needle to mark them.
Estimate the difference between the bregma and lambda along the dorsal-ventral axis using the needle.
Level the bregma and lambda along the dorsal-ventral axis by adjusting the dorsal/ventral adjustment dial of the stereotaxic.
Mark the point 1.94 mm posterior to the bregma.
Mark the target point 1.40 mm laterally from the point marked in step 6a.
Make four marks, one each in the anterior, posterior, medial, and lateral directions, 0.60 mm from the target point.
Drill a hole by mounting the drill bit on a micro hand drill.
Create a square-shaped opening in the skull by drilling (length of sides: ∼1.2 mm).
Verify that the lens fits into the opening.
Prepare virus injection by filling the Hamilton syringe with the virus (1 μL for each mouse).

Locate the injection site by placing the Hamilton syringe over one of the target sites (site 1, 1.94 mm posterior and 1.15 mm lateral to the bregma; site 2, 1.94 mm posterior and 1.6 mm lateral to the bregma).
Lower the Hamilton syringe to 1.1 mm below the brain surface, which is 0.05 mm above the target site.
Pause point: Wait 5 min for the brain tissue to stabilize.
Inject 0.4 μL of the virus at a rate of 0.05 μL/min.
Verify that the virus level in the Hamilton syringe decreases.
Remove the Hamilton syringe from the brain if the virus level does not decrease.
Gently clear the tip of the glass pipet with saline-soaked Cutanplast.
Cut the tip of the glass pipet slightly or replace it with a new one if clearing is ineffective.
Pause for 10 minutes after virus injection to allow the virus to spread in the brain tissue.
Move the Hamilton syringe upwards and repeat steps for the injection at the second site.
Seal the hole where the injection was made.
Blend the Kwik-Sil solution thoroughly.
Fill the hole with the blended Kwik-Sil mixture.
Wait 3 minutes for the Kwik-Sil mixture to set.
Suture the skin using a suture needle through the incision on both sides.
Tie a knot to close the skin incision securely.
Repeat steps of suturing until the skin is completely closed.
Wait for 2 weeks for viral expression before proceeding further.
Soak the head plate and screws in chlorhexidine gluconate solution for sterilization.
Align the head plate slightly in front of the coronal suture.
Use a micro hand drill to create an indentation on the skull beneath each screw hole.
Mark the location for another screw above the cerebellum.
Use a micro hand drill to make an indentation at the marked location.
Secure the head plate and the screw using a screwdriver.
Fasten the screws to barely penetrate the skull (less than 1 mm deep).
Remove the Kwik-Sil applied in step 9 to expose the hole.
Set up the suction setup.
Turn on the suction pump and set the vacuum pressure at over 50 kPa.
Place the suction needle tip on the brain tissue to be removed.
While absorbing, use an insulin syringe to apply saline to ensure a clear view and prevent blockage.
Remove brain tissue in the middle of the hole more deeply than at the edge, creating a funnel-shaped hollow by adjusting the angle of the suction needle.
Stop aspiration when white tissue (corpus callosum) appears.
Turn off the suction pump.
Absorb blood using Cutanplast.
Fill the hollow with saline-soaked Cutanplast.
Wait until bleeding stops.
Change the Cutanplast with a new one if it cannot absorb all of the blood.
Use Cutanplast to gently remove any remaining blood clots.
If bleeding resumes, apply Cutanplast until it stops.
Implant the lens.
Fix the dorsal lens holder to the stereotaxic holder.
Turn on the suction pump and increase vacuum pressure to more than 50 kPa.
Load the lens onto the tip assembly.
Align the center of the lens to the reference point 1.94 mm posterior and 1.4 mm lateral to the bregma.
Adjust the lens’ dorsal-ventral positioning using the skull as a reference.
Lower the lens to just above the skull.
Move the lens carefully to the medial side and confirm it is just above the skull.
Lower the lens to 1.7 mm below its previous position.
Lower the lens rapidly to 0.7 mm below its new position.
Slowly lower the lens an additional 1.0 mm at a speed of 0.2 mm/min.
Stop lowering the lens if blood begins to leak out of the hollow.
Absorb any minor bleeding with Cutanplast and wait for it to stop.
If significant bleeding occurs, lift the lens, clean it if necessary, absorb the blood with Cutanplast, and wait for bleeding to stop before continuing.
Fix the lens with cement.
Optional: If the hole is too large and the cortex is exposed between the lens and skull, fill the gap with Kwik-Sil.
Cover the lens, skull, head plate, and screw with Super Bond C&B.
Ensure the tip assembly is not covered with cement.
Switch off the suction pump.
Disconnect the lens holder from the suction pump to relieve pressure.
Remove the lens from the tip assembly.
Cover exposed portions of the skull, lens, head plate, and screw with additional dental cement if necessary.
Wait for the cement to harden for at least 10 minutes.
Apply Kwik-Cast to the lens.
Apply Kwik-Sil to cover the upper portion of the dental cement, including the area where Kwik-Cast has been applied.
Mark the point 3.16 mm posterior to the bregma.
Mark the target point 3.50 mm laterally from the point 18a.
Make four marks, one each in the anterior, posterior, medial, and lateral directions, 0.60 mm from the target point.
Drill a hole with sides reduced to about 0.8 mm.
Inject virus at two sites (3.16 mm posterior and 3.5 mm lateral to the bregma; 3.5 and 3.7 mm ventral to the brain surface).
Each injection has a volume of 0.3 μL, with an injection speed of 0.05 μL/min.
Pause point: Allow 10 min after virus injection for the virus to spread in the brain tissue.
Fix the head plate with screws.
Locate the lens target site.
Install the lens holder onto the stereotaxic holder.
Adjust the lens position as described in step 14e.
Position the GRIN lens to 3.16 mm posterior and 3.5 mm lateral to the bregma.
Lower the lens by 0.2 mm every 2 minutes, down to 2.0 mm from the brain surface.
Lower the lens by 0.1 mm every 2 minutes, down to 3.0 mm from the brain surface.
Lower the lens by 0.05 mm every 2 minutes, down to 3.6 mm from the brain surface.
Stop lowering the lens if blood begins to leak out during insertion.
Absorb blood with Cutanplast and wait for bleeding to stop before continuing.
Cover the lens, head plate, and screws with Super bond C&B.
Cover the first and second holes of the lens holder with Super bond C&B, but leave the third hole uncovered.
Disconnect the lens from the holder.
Gently cut the posterior side of the third hole in the lens holder with nippers.
Cut the anterior side of the third hole in the lens holder with nippers.
Apply cement again to the lens.
Cover the cut lens holder and make the dental cement surface rounded and smooth.
Use additional dental cement if necessary to cover exposed portions of the skull, lens, head plate, and screws.
Wait for the cement to harden for at least 10 minutes.
Apply Kwik-Cast and Kwik-Sil to the lens to prevent lens damage.
Wait for viral expression for 3–4 weeks.
Remove the Kwik-Sil and Kwik-Cast cover and clean the lens.
Remove the Kwik-Cast and Kwik-Sil using forceps.
Gently wipe the lens with a cotton swab soaked in 70% ethanol.
Find the focal plane of the microscope.
Set up the nVista system.
Assemble the baseplate and the Inscopix microscope.
Place the microscope above the lens.
Turn on the microscope’s light and move the microscope up and down until neurons are clearly visible.
Mark that position.
Surround the lens with black cement or black manicure to reduce light reflection around the lens.
Align the microscope to capture the largest number of active neurons in the focal plane.
Make a foundation for the baseplate.
Connect the foundation and the baseplate.
Cover the foundation with black manicure to prevent light noise.
Apply UV resin to the baseplate’s underside.
Harden the applied UV resin using a UV beam.
Add more resin to the spaces between the baseplate and the resin foundation.
Verify that the focal plane has not been changed.
Set the first focus of the microscope in the center of the focus range.
Use black manicure to conceal the foundation.
Cover the foundation’s exterior with black manicure to prevent light noise.
Cover the baseplate with a cover.
